# The formatting route sweep's per-stem census (FormattingRouteParitySweepTests.CensusFileName; #2512 W3.5, plan-88736c D3(i)).
#
# One row per (measure, twin, route, stem) with cells: measure twin route stem n # #issue
# measure — s7-parity-exempt: S7 recovery-misindented cells whose lost repair the clean twin loses too (lead ruling L7, #2279);
#           known-limit-S6k: the comment re-pair's string-content edits (#2274, R-FQ);
#           known-limit-S6ok: the unpairable own-quote tails' spurious facts (lead ruling L2, #2274);
#           refused-work: range cells with work that Format Selection declines (R-DK; tracked on #2538; identity, comment, wide only)
# twin    — identity | comment | wide | crlf | cr;  route — the routes the measure's state runs;  n — its cells (>= 1)
# Each twin's census asserts its rows exactly when its theory ran over every stem (SHARPY_ROUTE_SWEEP_PINS_REQUIRED=1 in CI):
# a missing row is a repair (or a gone stem), an extra one a new fact, a changed n a moved cell.
# GENERATED: bash build_tools/regenerate_corpus_pins.sh rewrites the rows; review the diff. A new fixture adds its own rows;
# a changed or missing row of an existing stem is a finding until explained (say which on the cited tracker). A red run
# after merging the base branch means a fixture landed there: run the same command. A stem above its route's refusal-ratio
# bound fails the run instead (formatting-route-refusal-exceptions.txt, hand-written).
